entry.title: Name what caught their attention
entry.summary: When your baby turns toward a sound or studies something nearby, give it a name and leave room for them to listen.
entry.cue: Their gaze settles on an object, or they turn when a familiar sound begins.
detail: A barking dog, a ringing phone or a spoon in your hand can start the conversation. Use the name you know and a few ordinary words about what is happening.
Follow the interest already there. The authors’ examples are shared noticing, not a request for the baby to repeat the word.

references.locator: Naming the ringing phone, barking dog and spoon in response to attention

ageContext.bookAge: Naming surroundings appears at 0 to 3 months; the detailed sound-and-object examples appear at 6 to 9 months.
ageContext.readiness: The baby’s attention settles on something you can name.
ageContext.note: Use the names you know. This is shared noticing, without asking the baby to repeat a word. Age and readiness sources: The Montessori Baby, PDF pp. 119–120, 130.

displayContext.footer: You don’t need a different home. Start with what you have.
displayContext.colophon: Original summaries inspired by The Montessori Baby and The Montessori Toddler. Open any idea for its book references. The illustration is an invitation to explore, rather than a room to reproduce. Follow your child’s pace.
displayContext.referenceNote: Paraphrased for this companion. Illustrations are original and illustrative.
